original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: Four scalar roles over F2[D8], paid labels the two involutions a,b, all 120 binary rank-one idempotents, and target diag([a],[ab],[ba],[e]); exact minimum paid length five.
scope_change_reason: The initially considered GL2(F2) four-role alphabet overlaps open PR #1763, which uses the same pair-state method for repeated order-three targets. The single bounded pivot changes the group to D8 and tests a heterogeneous reflection/order-four target; D8 PR #1742 covers a different three-role central-commutator target and states that four-role models remain open.
bottleneck_link: A four-factor identity would reduce this target's paid bit-word cost from five; supplier adoption still requires an actual source-word occurrence.
stop_rule: Enumerate every word of length at most four using exact full F2[D8] matrix products and verify the explicit five-factor upper word; stop after all pair-state meetings and controls.
evidence: verify.py: exact eight-element group algebra, all 240 factors, 32,651 ordered pair states, no word of length at most four, direct five-factor word and seven controls.
author: Cinna Davis, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human review is claimed.
